questions.prompt: What is the capital city of United States?

hints.nudge: It is 2 words long and starts with the letter W.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the United States article.

questions.proof: The capital city is Washington, D.C. and the largest city by population is New York, in the State of New York, with a population of 8.8 million people.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with United States?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter C and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the United States article.

questions.proof: Forty-eight of the states are connected (Contiguous United States), and they are bordered by Canada to the north and Mexico to the south.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of United States?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter H and has 8 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Language” part of the United States article.

questions.proof: Both Hawaiian and English are official languages in Hawaii by state law.

questions.prompt: What money is used in United States?

hints.nudge: It is 3 words long and starts with the letter U.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Money” part of the United States article.

questions.proof: The currency of the land is the United States dollar ($).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “All of these places have become independent: the _____ in 1946, Palau in 1947, and Micronesia in 1986.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter P and has 11 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Territories and possessions” part of the United States article.

questions.proof: All of these places have become independent: the Philippines in 1946, Palau in 1947, and Micronesia in 1986.
